_meta.purpose: Golden retrieval set for the Public Cloud Brain. Run before and after ANY change to the index, the embedding model, the chunker, or the metadata filters.
_meta.why_it_exists: The brain is shared infrastructure — the S4PC pipeline is only its first consumer. A retrieval change cannot be validated by 'the pipeline still ran'; a silently worse index still produces a confident deliverable. This set makes retrieval quality a measurable property instead of an assumption.
two_mechanisms: assertions — hand-written, encode INTENT ('a UI5 sorting question must reach developer_docs'). Few, durable, and they survive a full re-index because they key on `source`, not on chunk ids.
baseline snapshot — records what the brain returns today, so a later run can show DRIFT. Catches the regressions nobody thought to assert.
_meta.identity_note: Hits are identified by `chunk_file`. For SharePoint that is stable. For webdocs, doc_id is sha1(url) so it is stable per URL, but the _NNNN chunk suffix shifts if the upstream page is rewritten — that drift is legitimate and the report says so.
_meta.client_data_note: baseline.json is COMMITTED, and this repo is public. brain/ is gitignored precisely so client documents never reach git, so the baseline redacts them: `source` and `chunk_file` are stored verbatim only for source systems that are public by construction (developer_docs, sap_scope_catalog) and hashed for everything else. Overlap is computed on identity, not readability, so drift detection is unaffected. The allowlist in brain_regression.PUBLIC_SOURCE_SYSTEMS is closed — a new, unrecognised source is redacted rather than exposed. Caught on the first baseline run, which would otherwise have committed client cutover-plan and role-mapping filenames.

assertion_vocabulary.filters: dict passed straight to brain_search.search() — phase / agent_role / deliverable_type / source_system
assertion_vocabulary.expect_source_system: at least one hit carries this source_system
assertion_vocabulary.expect_absent_source_system: NO hit carries this source_system. Not the same claim as expect_no_hits — the SharePoint corpus answers almost any phase filter, so an exclusion has to be asserted per source, not as an empty result. The first baseline run caught R-041 making exactly that mistake.
assertion_vocabulary.expect_source_contains: at least one hit's `source` contains this substring (case-insensitive)
assertion_vocabulary.expect_min_hits: at least N hits come back
assertion_vocabulary.expect_no_hits: expect zero hits overall — only correct when the filter matches nothing in the entire corpus

cases.query: how do I sort and filter a list binding in a UI5 table
cases.why: FILTER CONTRACT — the multi-agent case, and the reason the provenance exemption exists. This case previously asserted the OPPOSITE (developer_docs absent), pinning the old behaviour so that changing it had to be deliberate. It was: PROVENANCE_EXEMPT_SOURCES now exempts vendor docs from phase/agent_role filters, because those fields describe which project phase produced an artifact and vendor docs were not produced by a project. A discovery agent asking phase=Explore must now reach the authoritative UI5 docs instead of getting a confident page of delivery documents with the real source missing.
